note: GSD release notes for every client (spec gsd-taskmanager/tasks/spec-whats-new.md, matrix row G8). The web repo is the authority: gsd-taskmanager/lib/whats-new/whats-new.json. Byte-identical copies ship inside the Apple and Android apps. Each client shows only its own platform's releases at or below its running version. notable true lets a release show the one-line post-update cue, and then headline is required. Write for users: what they can do now, one idea per item, nothing about dependencies, refactors, or tests.

releases.headline: See what changed in GSD, right in Settings.
new: Settings has a What's new section with the notes for every recent version, newest first. You can also open it from the command palette.
After an update with something new, one line under the matrix intro tells you what changed. Dismiss it and it stays gone.
fixed: Choosing Import tasks or Send feedback in the command palette now opens that section of Settings instead of Appearance.
When another device moves a task's due date, the web app now reminds you at the new time.
Snoozing a task before its reminder time no longer drops the reminder.

releases.headline: Save any web page to GSD with one click.
new: A bookmarklet in Settings turns the page you're reading into a task. Drag it to your bookmarks bar, with default tags if you like.
Nothing saves until you review the task and choose Create task.

improved: Settings now says that a copied AI assistant (MCP) token expires within 30 days, so you know when to copy a fresh one.

releases.headline: Stay signed in to sync for much longer.
improved: Sync sessions now last 30 days and renew on their own while you use GSD. Before, the web app could sign you out after a week even with daily use.
The self-hosted Docker image now uses 30-day sessions too.

releases.headline: Due times, snooze from anywhere, and a heads-up when tasks get close.
new: Give a due date a time of day. All-day tasks remind you at 9 a.m.
A task that isn't urgent can show as escalating as its due date gets close. Pick the window in Settings, or turn it off. Nothing moves until you choose Mark urgent.
Snooze a task from its card menu or the editor, and clear a snooze.
Duplicate a task, or move it to another quadrant, from the card menu.
On Android, share a link into the GSD web app from the share sheet.
improved: A reminder that falls in quiet hours now arrives when quiet hours end instead of being skipped.
Signing in with Apple now tells you which account you landed on.
fixed: New sync safeguards protect the tasks on this device, including a check before sync removes anything and safer imports.

releases.headline: Dozens of small fixes that make GSD easier to pick up.
improved: Due dates count calendar days, so "in 2 days" means what it says.
Dates stay in English and show the year when it isn't this year.
After you capture a task, GSD shows which quadrant it landed in.
Larger tap targets and clearer wording on phones and tablets.
Mark done is now in the task details sheet.
fixed: A double click or a repeated Enter no longer creates duplicate tasks.
Pasting several lines checks every line before adding any.
Back closes an open drawer or dialog, and GSD warns before a reload would lose unsaved changes.
After this update, the first sync brings your Saved items to every device, including tasks synced before Saved existed.

releases.headline: Introducing Saved: a place for reading and reference outside the matrix.
new: Saved holds links, reading, and reference notes outside the matrix, so they stay out of your priorities until you need them.
Saved items sync with the iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Android apps.
The GSD connector for AI assistants (MCP server 1.4.0) can read and manage Saved items.

improved: Security updates to the libraries GSD depends on.
Clearer labels on the Review page, a short introduction in Settings, and a plain description of who runs the sync server.

releases.headline: Each quadrant now scrolls on its own, and large text works everywhere.
new: The matrix fits your screen, and each quadrant scrolls by itself, so a long list in one quadrant no longer pushes the others out of view.
improved: GSD follows your browser's text size and reflows instead of scrolling sideways.
Better keyboard, touch, and screen reader support, with stronger contrast throughout.
Buttons in the task drawer are sized for touch.
fixed: iPhone Safari no longer zooms in when you tap into the editor or the command palette.

releases.headline: Due times, and reminders you can act on.
new: Set a time of day on a due date. All-day tasks remind you at 9 a.m.
Reminders have Complete and Snooze 1 hour buttons, so you can act without opening the app.
A task that isn't urgent can show as escalating as its due date gets close. Pick the window in Settings, or turn it off. Nothing moves until you choose Mark urgent.
improved: The task editor asks before discarding changes, and only when you made some.
With a keyboard, ⌘S saves the task from any field. On iPad, ⌘? opens Help.
On Mac, Trash has a right-click menu to restore or delete a task.
The matrix shows a placeholder while your tasks load instead of a blank screen.
fixed: Several fixes protect the tasks on your device during sync and when you delete your account.
On iPad and Mac, a quadrant with a single task no longer stretches that card to fill the space.
After this update, your Saved items sync correctly, including tasks synced before Saved existed.

releases.headline: Saved arrives, with a fresh look for iOS 27 and macOS 27.
new: Saved holds reading and reference outside the matrix, with short notes, and syncs with the web and Android apps.
A refreshed look built for iOS 27 and macOS 27.
A large Today's Focus widget.
Quadrant completion rings, deadline badges, and search in Browse.
A 30-day Trash, so you can restore deleted tasks.
Backups that keep every detail of your tasks.
An optional, anonymous feedback form that shows you exactly what it sends.
improved: Tasks you share from Safari or other apps reach your other devices right away instead of waiting until you open GSD.
GSD syncs and picks up shared tasks during background refresh.
Support for iPhone Duo, and upside-down portrait on iPhone.
Better layouts at large accessibility text sizes.
fixed: Archiving a task removes its synced copy, so it can't reappear on another device.

releases.headline: Saved, escalation, and pull to sync.
new: Saved holds reading and reference outside the matrix, with short notes, and syncs with the web and Apple apps.
Tasks due soon can show as escalating, with a Mark urgent action and a setting for the window.
Pull down on the Matrix to sync, on phones and tablets.
The Dashboard shows the completion rate for your top 8 tags.
Sync history shows totals.
improved: All-day tasks remind you at 9 a.m. on the due day.
fixed: Safer sync that protects Saved items, new tasks, and edits, even when a device clock is wrong.

releases.headline: Due times, a new welcome tour, and a more polished app.
new: Set a due time, or mark a task all day.
A new welcome tour, Field Guide, and About page.
Swipe left on a task for Snooze and Delete.
improved: GSD asks for notification permission the first time a reminder needs it, and Settings can allow exact alarms.
The editor keeps Save at the top and asks before discarding edits.
Shared links open over the app you shared from.
Better TalkBack support, stronger text contrast, and fixes for tablets and landscape.
Your tasks stay out of Android cloud backup.
Swipe to complete or delete works on every task list, not only the Matrix.
Completing a task celebrates it on every list.
Settings tells you when your sync session has expired.
fixed: Switching sync accounts keeps the tasks on your device.
Tapping a reminder opens the task from any tab.
